subject: Seoul pilot + Frankfurt buffer — tranche fulfillment & node reserve matrix
messages:

Cc: Procurement <procurement@nebulasys.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity ask — Seoul pilot + Frankfurt buffer for Q3 pilot

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Nebula is preparing a Q3 pilot (1 month) for our conversational search stack and we need a dedicated lane for APAC (Seoul) plus a compliance-aware buffer in EU (Frankfurt) during the pilot window. High-level ask below so the team can sanity-check:

- Target start: 2026-07-15
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~1,200 (inference requests/minute)
- Model profile: medium transformer (approx. 16B unquantized), typical sequence length 512 tokens
- Expected burst lanes: +40% for first 2 weeks of pilot
- Data residency: EU traffic must ingress to Frankfurt pool for recording/audit scope

Can you confirm lead times and whether a small reserved pool + burst lanes is doable? Attached is our traffic profile (Nebula_traffic_profile_Q3.xlsx).

Appreciate a quick sanity check so procurement can draft SOW.

—Ryan Mendoza
Director of Platform Ops
Nebula Systems

Subject: Re: Capacity ask — Seoul pilot + Frankfurt buffer for Q3 pilot

Ryan — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Looping in capacity and sourcing. Quick clarifying Qs from our side:

1) Is the 1,200 req/min peak sustained across 24h or concentrated in a 4–6 hr daily window?
2) Do you need node pinning for audit (i.e., all EU traffic always served from FRA) or is logical routing sufficient with audit logs?
3) Are you open to an initial conservative commit and then an automatic burst policy for the first two weeks?

Internal: Karthik/Hannah, can you run a sketch on node counts by region and an estimated tranche (commit + burst) timeline? Ben/Laura, flag any procurement/legal lead time constraints we should account for in the MAP.

Thanks — I’ll consolidate and share a brief mutual action plan once we have numbers.

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ryan Mendoza <ryan.mendoza@nebulasys.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity ask — Seoul pilot + Frankfurt buffer for Q3 pilot

Marissa / team / Ryan — ran a quick sizing exercise with ops assumptions for the 16B workload:

Assumptions: average token generation 120 tokens/req, 512 sequence budget for KV cache sizing, quantization not assumed for pilot.

Suggested starting configuration (conservative):
- APAC (Seoul) reserved: 6 GPU nodes (A100-equivalent) — steady throughput ~800 req/min; with automatic batching can meet ~1,200 req/min with 40% burst using pre-warmed burst lanes (2 additional nodes)
- EU (Frankfurt) reserved (compliance buffer): 3 GPU nodes — handles low steady EU traffic and audit capture; route EU production traffic to FRA nodes only (logical routing + mandatory audit logs)
- US standby: 2 nodes for failover/fallback (not primary for pilot)

Tradeoffs: If Nebula accepts 8-bit quantization we can reduce required nodes by ~30% (operationally faster to provision if willing). Lead time: procurement & SOW + security review ~3–5 weeks; physical node provisioning (if Dedicated) 4–6 weeks depending on region availability.

I attached a draft SKU tiling PDF with the node math (initial_sku_tiling_v1.pdf). If they want hard pinning for EU, we need to size FRA for peak plus safety buffer which would increase FRA to 5 nodes.

—Karthik
Director, Deals Strategy
Redwood Inference

Ryan / team — procurement & legal notes:

- Procurement timeline (best case): 3 weeks for MA + SOW if standard RD clauses accepted. If we need additional data processing addendum or bespoke retention language, add 1–2 weeks.
- Compliance: for EU-resident logging we will enable FRA routing and an audit-only retention window; needs explicit acknowledgement in SOW.
- CloudSupply (cc’d) can expedite hardware fulfillment if Nebula opts for a burst contract (we have a channel agreement that shortens physical provisioning to ~2 weeks in some APAC carriers).

Ben/Laura — we should draft a mutual action plan and identify the SOW owner. Ryan, please confirm which retention SLA (30/90/365 days) you need for audit artifacts.

Subject: Re: Capacity ask — Seoul pilot + Frankfurt buffer for Q3 pilot

Marissa / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the numbers. Answers:

- The 1,200 req/min is concentrated in a 6hr regional window (09:00–15:00 KST) — not 24h sustained.
- For EU audit we prefer hard pinning (FRA) for the recordings during the pilot. Retention: 90 days is our target.
- Nebula is open to a small quantization step if Redwood certifies outputs are within our quality threshold (we’ll run a quick eval).

Procurement will push MA + SOW once sizing is confirmed. We can accept a commit + burst contract. Attached is a revised traffic workbook (updated numbers). If you can send a MAP with dates/owners we’ll align on sign-off timelines.

Best,
Ryan
